clue.text: Defeat attributed to stealth war tactics

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A military analyst credits a defeat to the enemy's sneaky tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart a plan is to frustrate or foil it, a verb synonym of defeat.

clue.text: Essentially they vacuously cheek live routines

definitions.text: Essentially they vacuously cheek live routines

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters of the next word are kept
emptied of content, each of the following words keeps just its shell of first and last letters

explanation.surface: Some people mindlessly interrupt and mock performers mid-act with empty insults.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes HECKLERS, who shout empty cheek at live acts; read as wordplay, it takes the middle of one word and the outsides of the next three.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecklers are audience members who interrupt performers with jeering remarks, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Transport belied description of fare

indicators.note: to transport things is to move them about, so the letters of the next word are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A travel company's service fails to live up to its own advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price, which fits 'Transport', but here it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible is the adjective you apply to food that is fit to eat, so it describes fare in the sense of meals.

clue.text: Scotsman leaves kind of restaurant catering for Rastafarian

indicators.note: when someone leaves a place he is no longer in it, so his name is taken out of the word

blocks.note: a restaurant serving food from Italy
Ian is the stock Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scottish diner walks out of a restaurant that serves Rastafarian customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ital food is the natural, largely vegetarian diet followed by Rastafarians.
explanation.definitionFit: Ital is the name of the food and cooking prescribed by Rastafarian dietary principles, so it is their catering.

clue.text: Creature of deep gold, lit up in rising sun

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading a word from the bottom
a word rising in a down light is read from bottom to top
one group of letters sits inside another

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A deep-sea creature glints gold as the dawn sun lights it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautilus is a shelled cephalopod mollusc that lives in the deep ocean.

clue.text: Rubbish review created issue around book

B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A scathing review of some trash stirred up trouble about a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish review' reads as a bad critique; 'Rubbish' is the definition and 'review' the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris means scattered waste or remains, a noun synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Birdie beat low score, taking one stroke less, to go into lead

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
going into the lead puts this piece in front of the other one

blocks.note: in golf, the score two under par, one stroke fewer than a birdie

explanation.surface: A golfer's birdie is outdone when a rival shoots a lower score, one shot better, and moves ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all golf, but 'Birdie' is a playful word for a bird and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle owl is a very large owl of Europe and Asia, and birdie is a familiar word for any bird.

clue.text: Connecting line passing through South Reading

indicators.note: the answer runs through the following words, crossing the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A railway line that runs through the southern part of Reading, a Berkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread is a fine strand, and figuratively the line of argument that connects ideas together.

clue.text: Call to move quickly over evidence of unbalanced economy

explanation.surface: A shout to hurry along about signs that an economy is out of kilter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap, where imports exceed exports, is a standard indicator that a country's economy is out of balance.

clue.text: This animal's bulk will shatter on the rocks

explanation.surface: A heavy creature washed onto a reef will be smashed to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shatter' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'on the rocks' does the job, and suits a sea animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawksbill turtle is a sea turtle of tropical reefs, named for its hooked, beak-like mouth.

clue.text: Airy acknowledgement others helped to wrap present

indicators.note: a wrapping goes all around its contents, so one piece encloses the other

present in the sense of in attendance

explanation.walkthrough: 'present' suggests a gift being wrapped; it means here, in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means light and delicate, as if made of air, so it is an adjective synonym of airy.

clue.text: Song about man's bottom displaying signs of age

indicators.note: the bottom of a word written down is its final letter
one piece goes about, surrounding, the other

blocks.note: a lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: A cheeky song about a man's backside showing the effects of ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lined face is wrinkled, which is a typical visible effect of growing older.

clue.text: Reading is not so busy

blocks.note: less is the comparative meaning to a smaller degree
on, as in engaged or in progress

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the town of Reading is quieter than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the Berkshire town, but it is a reading from scripture in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a passage from the Bible read aloud during a church service, also called a reading.

clue.text: Emergency credit's withdrawn where one might take a punt

definitions.text: where one might take a punt

blocks.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.walkthrough: 'take a punt' suggests a wager; here a punt is a flat boat. The Isis is the stretch of the Thames at Oxford, famous for punting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the name for the River Thames as it flows through Oxford, where students go punting.

clue.text: Enhanced thus, one produces paper at university before and after

indicators.note: the same piece is used twice, once on each side of the middle piece

blocks.note: up, as in in residence at college
ed is short for editor, who produces a newspaper

explanation.surface: A student editor brings out a newspaper while at university.
explanation.walkthrough: To be up at a university is the British phrase for being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: Souped-up means modified to give more power or performance, as with a car's engine, hence enhanced.

clue.text: American intelligence takes precedence in class

indicators.note: to take precedence is to go first, so this piece is put ahead of the other

explanation.surface: American spies get priority when the classification is decided.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a biological rank grouping related species, so it is a class or kind of things.

clue.text: Saw claims that this warrants repetition

definitions.text: Saw claims that this warrants repetition

blocks.clueFragment: Saw claims that this warrants repetition

setter's reading: a saw is a proverb, the one saying a kindly act deserves another

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'one good turn deserves another', so the saw claims this act warrants repeating.
explanation.definitionFit: A good turn is a helpful favour done for someone, and the old proverb says such a favour should be repaid.

clue.text: Doctor swallows contents of pill having little effect

clue.text: Diplomat representing Catholic Union

clue.text: In recession, city banks reluctant to invest

clue.text: In favour of meeting requirements for benefit

explanation.surface: Supporting a plan because it satisfies all the needs for a welfare payment.

clue.text: Maintain code not requiring recompilation or debugging?

clue.text: Tailor made something to drink

explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic beverage brewed from fermented honey and water.

clue.text: Spooner's express disapproval of idiot is worth little

explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is an American adjective for cheap or insignificant, from the old slang for a quarter dollar.
